## `balance_column`: projection of a ghost-free column onto the scheme's discrete balance (C++ and Python API) {#sec-ch05-balcol}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Moves a column of cell averages, at fixed $p/\rho$ per cell, to the fixed point
$\overline p=p_{\mathrm{ref}}(\overline p)+C$ of @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest, so that the solver starts it at rest.
**Switch.** None: an API function, `balance_column` in C++ and in the Python package, called by initial-condition
builders. Requires `wb-wall-clamp` on, at least five cells, positive $p$ and $\rho$.
**Order.** Fixed point to a residual below `rtol` (default $10^{-10}$, at most 120 sweeps).
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-balcol-iter.
:::

A column integrated from the continuum hydrostatic equation is balanced to the truncation error of that integration,
not to the scheme's own discrete balance. The well-balanced reconstruction then sees a perturbation $p'$ that is not
constant and turns its variation into a standing force on an atmosphere that should be at rest. `balance_column`
removes that force before the run starts: it iterates the column onto the discrete rest state, holding the
temperature of each cell fixed for ideal mixtures, and returns the balanced column, the residual and the number of
updates. The fixed point is defined only up to a free constant $C$, so the column moves; any pinned quantity (surface
pressure, column mass) has to be re-pinned by the caller.

Under `SNAP_WB_REF4` on a non-uniform grid it iterates against the switched cell pressure, which is the fixed point
the solver then enforces. Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` it balances only a column declared Cartesian.

*Aliases.* "the balance-ic projection" (the bryan example's `balance-ic`), chengcli/snapy#250 D1.

### Derivation

Units as in @sec-ch05-wbx1. Let the column hold $n_1\ge5$ cells with no ghosts and both ends physical, and let
$\theta_i=\overline p_i/\overline\rho_i$ be taken once from the input. One sweep evaluates the reference kernel on the
whole column, reads the gauge at the top cell and updates

$$
\begin{aligned}
C &= \overline{p}_{n_1-1} - p_{\mathrm{ref},n_1-1}, \\
\overline{p}_i &\leftarrow p_{\mathrm{ref},i}(\overline{p},\overline{\rho}) + C, \\
\overline{\rho}_i &\leftarrow \overline{p}_i/\theta_i ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-balcol-iter}

and stops when

$$
\varepsilon = \max_i\frac{\lvert \overline{p}_i - p_{\mathrm{ref},i} - C\rvert}{\overline{\rho}_i\,g\,\Delta x_{1,i}} < \mathrm{rtol} .
$$ {#eq-ch05-balcol-res}

The sweep @eq-ch05-balcol-iter and the stop test @eq-ch05-balcol-res are the loop that calls `call_hydro_ref_x1`
([`balance_column.cpp:85-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L85-L104)).
A fixed point of @eq-ch05-balcol-iter satisfies @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest with $c=C$, so it is at rest in the solver. The
residual is checked before the update, so the returned column is the one it describes and an already balanced
column comes back after zero updates. $\varepsilon$ bounds the residual acceleration in units of $g$: a perturbation
difference $\delta p'$ across a cell drives an acceleration $\delta p'/(\overline\rho\Delta x_1)$.

The gauge is read at the top cell, where the pressure is lowest, so the column moves least where it is thinnest; the
code comment records that a gauge at the bottom diverges on a deep column. Holding $\theta_i$ fixed holds the
temperature fixed for `ideal-gas` and for `ideal-moist` at fixed mass fractions. No convergence proof exists; the
sweep is a contraction in practice, and the check shows it on a column that is not balanced to begin with
(`[C15]`: a $\beta=0.3$ polytrope with a $10^{-3}$ pressure bump at fixed $p/\rho$, $n_1=64$, residual
$4.64\times10^{-2}$ to $1.03\times10^{-11}$ in 12 updates, $p/\rho$ unchanged to $1.5\times10^{-16}$).

*Why the result transfers to the blocks.* With the wall clamp on, the reference of a block's interior reads only owned
cells at a physical wall (@sec-ch05-wallclamp), so a ghost-free column and a block holding the same cells get the same
$p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, bitwise; that is what the first test below asserts. Without the clamp the wall rows read ghost
faces that the ghost-free column does not have, and the two disagree, which is why the function refuses to run.
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ differs at the bottom cell only (its fallback keys on the array index), and it plays no part in
the fixed point.

*Exact and truncated.* The returned column satisfies @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest to $\varepsilon<\mathrm{rtol}$; nothing is
truncated beyond that.

### Numerical method

What the projection does is shown in @fig-ch05-balcol-gauge. Each sweep is one call of the reference kernel on the column
(CPU, CUDA or MPS, with the column's device), plus the switched cell pressure of @sec-ch05-wbref4 when that switch is on
and the column is non-uniform; uniformity is decided with the solver's test on the column's own widths.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-balcol-gauge
#| fig-cap: "What `balance_column` does to a column, $x_1$ to the right. Vermillion dashed circles: the perturbation $p - p_{\\mathrm{ref}}$ [Pa] of a column marched from the continuum equation, which varies along the column; bluish-green squares: after the projection it is one constant $C$ [Pa], the value at the top cell. The column itself moves by $C$ everywhere. Illustrative values."
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a wavy dashed curve of circles and a flat line of squares meeting at the right end, with an arrow labelling the right end as the gauge."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.fig_balcol_gauge import make_fig
make_fig()
```

A moist initial condition needs one more loop. The projection holds the mass fractions fixed, and the run's first
saturation adjustment moves the column off the balance again. The bryan example's `balance-ic` therefore alternates
saturation and projection until saturation no longer moves the projected column (relative density change at most
$4\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}$ and $\max\lvert\Delta p/p\rvert\le10^{-13}$), within `balance-ic-passes`
(@fig-ch05-balcol-passes).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-balcol-passes
#| fig-cap: "The moist balance-ic loop of the bryan example, per pass. (a) Largest relative pressure change $\\max\\lvert\\Delta p/p\\rvert$ [-] the saturation adjustment makes to the column just projected (bluish-green circles); the dotted line is the stop criterion $10^{-13}$. (b) Projection sweeps `balance_column` needed in that pass (black squares). The change falls by about a factor 20 per pass and the loop stops after pass 6."
#| fig-alt: "Two panels: a semilog plot falling linearly over six passes below a dotted threshold line, and a plot of sweeps falling from 13 to 4."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.fig_balcol_passes import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of `balance_column`. {#tbl-ch05-balcol-code}

1. The arguments are checked: $g>0$, shape, matching widths, positive `rtol` and `max_iter`, the clamp, and the
   geometry under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, each with a `TORCH_CHECK`
   ([`balance_column.cpp:18-40`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L18-L40)).
2. The column length `nc1` must be at least 5 and $p$, $\rho$ positive; $\theta_i$ is stored
   ([`balance_column.cpp:42-55`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L42-L55)).
3. Uniformity is decided and, for a switched non-uniform column, the stencils of @sec-ch05-wbref4 are built into
   the flag `ref4`
   ([`balance_column.cpp:65-79`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L65-L79)).
4. The loop runs @eq-ch05-balcol-res and @eq-ch05-balcol-iter, counting `sweeps`, and raises if the pressure turns
   non-positive
   ([`balance_column.cpp:85-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L85-L104)).
5. A residual `err` still above `rtol` raises
   ([`balance_column.cpp:106-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L106-L108)).

Errors a user can hit: the clamp off, fewer than five cells, a non-positive input, a spherical-polar geometry under
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, a diverging column, and no convergence within `max_iter`. The caller also owns four
conditions the function cannot check, listed in its header: physical $x_1$ ends, at least five cells per block of the
later run, the same uniform classification in every block, and the saturation loop for moist columns.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The balanced column moves by a free constant: the header of `balance_column.hpp` quotes $2.5\times10^{-4}$ of $p$ on a Neptune-like column
and $1.2\times10^{-2}$ on a 300 km giant-planet one (no deck given; not re-measured). A spherical-polar column cannot be
balanced under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`.
:::

1. **Free gauge.** Nothing ties the result to the input's surface pressure or mass; callers re-pin inside their own
   loop.
2. **Classification.** The uniform test is made once for the whole column and must match every block's own test.
3. **Moist columns.** The caller must iterate with saturation adjustment, as the bryan example does.
4. **No convergence proof.** Convergence is observed (`[C15]`, the tests), not proven.
5. **Untested combinations.** See the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
